answer.reason: The verses give several events of Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz: his message in Hezekiah's sickness, the sign of the shadow, and his walking naked and barefoot as a sign.

clauses.english: told the sick King Hezekiah he would die, then was sent back to say he would be healed
clauses.quote: Set thine house in order; for thou shalt die, and not live.

clauses.english: cried to the LORD and the shadow went back ten degrees on the dial of Ahaz
clauses.quote: Isaiah the prophet cried unto the LORD: and he brought the shadow ten degrees backward

clauses.english: walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign upon Egypt and Ethiopia
clauses.quote: my servant Isaiah hath walked naked and barefoot three years for a sign and wonder

doubts: The verses cited from the New Testament name Esaias, which is the Greek form of Isaiah, but they only quote his words, so they were not used.
The sending of messengers to Isaiah by Hezekiah and his prayer with the king (2CH 32:20) were left out as lesser events.
